text:
lia: Heads up — seeing a big latency surge on prod inference since the infra deploy 20m ago (CUDA 12.2 + driver bump). p50/p95 jumped ~3x.

omar: Saw the alert. Which cluster/region?

lia: us-west-2 pool-rt-gpu-4. Affected routes: /v1/generate-heavy and chat-stream. Throughput dropped too.

infra-bot: Deploy completed by @deploy-bot (deploy/infra/cuda-driver-update), id=deploy-2026-03-18-01. Rolling to all gpu pools.

jay: Can you paste a couple of traces from the runtime profiler?

lia: Paste: 
```
[2026-03-18T01:12:04Z] runtime/dispatch selected_kernel=matmul_fused_sm80_v3 (latency_est=9ms)
[2026-03-18T01:12:04Z] runtime/dispatch fallback_kernel=matmul_cuBLAS (latency_est=25ms)
[2026-03-18T01:12:05Z] batcher: batch_size=8 -> 4 (backpressure)
[2026-03-18T01:12:07Z] kvcache: active_entries=1.2M evicted=320k lru_evictions=318k
[2026-03-18T01:12:07Z] gpu-metrics: memcpy_htod=4.2ms memcpy_dtoh=5.8ms kernel_exec=18.4ms (prev driver: kernel_exec=6.1ms)
```

maria: That kernel_exec jump is huge. Looks like the fused attention kernel isn't being used and we're falling back to a slower path. Could be Triton/kernel selection mismatch after driver change.

omar: Reproduced on staging with same driver. nsys shows heavy time in memcpy and kernel stalls. Snippet: 
```
== Major time consumers ==
1) kernel: gemm_fallback (67%)
2) cudaMemcpy (18%)
3) kernel: kv_cache_handle (9%)
```

jay: Any driver-level warnings in dmesg or CUDA logs?

lia: dmesg contains repeated: 
```
[GPU0] cuBLAS version mismatch: expected 12.1.x, loaded 12.2.x - some kernels relocated
```

lia: Also saw lines from Triton loader: `no compatible fused kernel for arch=sm80, fallback to generic`

omar: Looks like the binary kernels we ship (precompiled fused kernels for sm80) are failing the compatibility check, so the runtime selects generic kernels. That explains both higher kernel time and increase in memcpy if we fall back to less fused layout.

maria: Two possible mitigations: 1) pin driver to previous version (rollback) 2) force runtime to prefer our legacy kernel bundle using an override env var (runtime.experimental.force_kernel_bundle=legacy-sm80). Which is faster to do?

jay: Rolling back driver across all pools is risky but fastest to restore perf. Forcing kernel bundle requires testing; might cause correctness issues if API/ABI changed.

lia: Quick test: set env override on a single canary node (pool-rt-gpu-4-canary). I pushed config and restarted runtime on one pod. Result: p95 dropped from ~230ms -> ~80ms for same load.

omar: Good. What's the rollback window?

sre-oncall: We can roll back the driver in a coordinated 15-min maintenance; need change freeze for customer-facing endpoints. I can schedule if we decide.

lia: Left more profiling: nvprof/nvtx tags show fused_attention kernel missing from module list. Search in /opt/runtime/kernels: most .cubin files have newer build id.

maria: Hypothesis: CUDA 12.2 driver introduced a minor PTX verifier change that rejects some precompiled cubins we ship, causing selection logic -> fallback. Action items: rebuild kernel bundle with 12.2 toolchain and release, and meanwhile rollback driver.

omar: Also noticed KV cache eviction spike. Likely caused by slower kernel leading to longer in-flight tensors occupying GPU memory -> LRU evictions. That aggravates tail latencies due to cache cold-starts.

lia: I grabbed a small trace of request lifecycle: 
```
request_id=abc123: enqueue->start(12ms) gpu_alloc(4ms) kv_lookup_cache_miss -> populate(22ms) kernel_exec(19ms) finish
vs
prev stable: enqueue->start(3ms) gpu_alloc(1ms) kv_lookup_cache_hit -> kernel_exec(6ms) finish
```

maria: That kv_cache_miss rate jump matches the evicted count in logs. Need to monitor mem pressure metric and consider raising kvcache reservation per pod temporarily.

jay: For immediate runbook:
- rollback driver to 12.1 across prod pools (sre to schedule)
- enable runtime.experimental.force_kernel_bundle=legacy-sm80 on canaries to verify safety
- build new kernel bundle against 12.2 and run full test suite (perf + correctness)
- increase kvcache reservation on hot routes to reduce LRU churn

omar: I can start the kernel rebuild in CI (queued). Estimated 4-6h for validated build.

lia: I'll open a postmortem stub and tag root cause as driver-compatibility -> kernel-selection fallback -> kvcache eviction cascade.

infra-bot: Change request created: CR-2987 (rollback cuda-driver -> 12.1), owner=@sre-oncall, impact=medium, ETA=15m to start.

sre-oncall: Starting rollback now on us-west-2, canary -> batch. Will report when p95 stabilizes.

omar: One more data point: Affected models are long-context attention (Llama-variant). Short-context embedding calls not impacted much.

lia: thanks all. Ping me if p95 doesn't come down after rollback. :eyes:

maria: After rollback confirmation we should add an automated compatibility test: load each kernel cubin under each driver version in CI to prevent this regression.

jay: Agreed — add to kernel onboarding checklist and gate driver upgrades behind canary perf checks. :+1:
